lessons.title: Excretion, water balance and skin glands

scenes.say: In freshwater Paramecium, a contractile vacuole inside the cell periodically empties excess water to the outside. In many insects, Malpighian tubules open into the gut and help remove nitrogenous waste as uric acid or urates, saving water.

A coiled sweat gland under the skin sends sweat, containing salts and a little urea, up a duct to a pore. A sebaceous gland beside a hair follicle releases oily sebum into the follicle to lubricate hair and skin.
Plants can store tannins in tissues such as bark. Tannins bind proteins and are used to turn hides into leather.
JAMB asks what the contractile vacuole expels, which nitrogenous waste conserves water in many insects, and which skin glands release sebum. Blue arrows follow water or waste. Amber follows sebum.

quickCheck.prompt: Which Paramecium structure pumps excess water out?
quickCheck.feedback: The contractile vacuole gathers and periodically expels excess water.
